entries.title: Strength
entries.whatItMeans: Strength measures physical power, force, and raw muscle.
entries.exampleInPlay: A character with high Strength might shove open a heavy door, wrestle an enemy to the ground, or haul a fallen ally out of danger.
entries.whyItMatters: If your character fights up close, does physical tasks, or relies on brute force, Strength matters a lot.

entries.title: Dexterity
entries.whatItMeans: Dexterity measures agility, reflexes, balance, and fine control.
entries.exampleInPlay: A character with high Dexterity might dodge a trap, move silently through a hallway, or shoot a bow with precision.
entries.whyItMatters: Dexterity affects defense, speed, sneaking, and many common combat actions, so it is useful for a wide range of characters.

entries.title: Constitution
entries.whatItMeans: Constitution measures toughness, endurance, and the ability to keep going when things get rough.
whatItAffects: Resistance to sickness, exhaustion, and bodily strain
entries.exampleInPlay: A character with high Constitution might stay standing after a brutal hit, shrug off poison, or keep a spell going under pressure.
entries.whyItMatters: Constitution helps a character survive longer in danger, especially in combat or harsh environments.

entries.title: Intelligence
entries.whatItMeans: Intelligence measures reasoning, memory, study, and analysis.
entries.exampleInPlay: A character with high Intelligence might identify a magical sigil, piece together clues from a ruined library, or recognize an old kingdom from a symbol on a shield.
entries.whyItMatters: Intelligence is useful when your character learns from books, clues, research, or careful thinking.

entries.title: Wisdom
entries.whatItMeans: Wisdom measures awareness, intuition, and a character's sense of what is happening around them.
entries.exampleInPlay: A character with high Wisdom might notice an ambush before it happens, sense that someone is lying, or find a safe path through the wilderness.
entries.whyItMatters: Wisdom helps a character notice danger, read people, and stay grounded in uncertain situations.

entries.title: Charisma
entries.whatItMeans: Charisma measures force of personality, confidence, charm, and presence.
entries.exampleInPlay: A character with high Charisma might talk their way past a guard, command a room, or cast powerful spells through sheer force of personality.
entries.whyItMatters: Charisma matters when your character influences other people, leads, negotiates, or uses certain types of magic.

entries.title: Armor Class
entries.whatItMeans: Armor Class, or AC, is the number an attacker must meet or beat to hit your character.
whatItAffects: How difficult your character is to injure
entries.exampleInPlay: If your AC is 16 and an enemy rolls a 14 plus 3 for a total of 17, the attack hits. If they roll 12 plus 3 for 15, the attack misses.
entries.whyItMatters: Armor Class is one of the main defenses in combat. Higher AC generally means your character is harder to hit.

entries.title: Initiative
entries.whatItMeans: Initiative determines when your character acts at the start of combat.
whatItAffects: Who acts first when combat starts
entries.exampleInPlay: When combat begins, everyone rolls initiative. The highest result goes first, then the next highest, and so on.
entries.whyItMatters: Acting earlier can help your character control the fight, protect allies, or strike before enemies do.

entries.title: Speed
entries.whatItMeans: Speed tells you how far your character can move during their turn, usually measured in feet.
whatItAffects: How far you can move on your turn
entries.exampleInPlay: If your speed is 30 feet, you can usually move up to 30 feet on your turn, then still take your actions.
entries.whyItMatters: Speed affects mobility, tactical positioning, and whether your character can reach what they need in a fight or scene.

entries.title: Hit Points
entries.whatItMeans: Hit Points, or HP, represent how much punishment your character can take before falling.
whatItAffects: When your character is knocked unconscious
How much damage you can absorb
entries.exampleInPlay: If your character has 12 hit points and takes 7 damage, they now have 5 hit points left.
entries.whyItMatters: HP is one of the clearest measures of how long a character can stay in the fight.

entries.title: Passive Perception
entries.whatItMeans: Passive Perception is what your character notices without actively rolling to search.
whatItAffects: What your character picks up naturally
entries.exampleInPlay: If a trap is hidden in a hallway, your Passive Perception might determine whether you notice it before stepping on it.
entries.whyItMatters: Passive Perception helps the game move quickly when the DM wants to know whether a character notices something automatically.

entries.title: Proficiency Bonus
entries.whatItMeans: Proficiency Bonus is the number added to things your character is trained or especially good at.
whatItAffects: Skill checks you are proficient in
Saving throws you are proficient in
Spell save DC and spell attack bonus for casters
entries.exampleInPlay: If your proficiency bonus is +2 and you are proficient in a skill, you add +2 to that skill check before other modifiers.
entries.whyItMatters: Proficiency Bonus scales with level and is one of the core numbers behind almost everything your character does well.

entries.title: Spell Save DC
entries.whatItMeans: Spell Save DC is the number enemies must meet or beat on a saving throw to resist one of your spells.
entries.exampleInPlay: If your Spell Save DC is 14, a creature must roll 14 or higher on its saving throw to resist the spell's effect.
entries.whyItMatters: A higher Spell Save DC makes your spells harder to resist.

entries.title: Spell Attack Bonus
entries.whatItMeans: Spell Attack Bonus is the number added when you make a spell attack roll.
entries.exampleInPlay: If your spell attack bonus is +5 and you roll a 12, your total spell attack roll is 17.
entries.whyItMatters: A higher spell attack bonus makes it easier for attack spells to hit their target.
